Latent class analysis

lca.Rd

Fits a latent class model to categorical indicators by maximum likelihood (EM algorithm) with Mplus-style random starts, optionally with one-step covariates (latent class regression), sampling weights or known groups (multigroup LCA with full, partial or no measurement invariance).

Usage

lca(
  data,
  items,
  K,
  starts = c(100, 20),
  covariates = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  invariance = "full",
  device = "cpu",
  seed = 20261119,
  maxiter = 5000,
  tol = 1e-10,
  cluster = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  optseed = NULL,
  level2 = NULL,
  KB = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  between_covariates = NULL,
  integration = 15,
  adaptive = TRUE,
  direct = NULL,
  classspecific = NULL,
  pairs = NULL,
  association = "varying",
  slopes = "equal",
  polish = TRUE,
  proportions = "free"
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or matrix (one row per respondent). Indicators may be factors, characters, logicals, labelled vectors or numeric category codes; NA marks a missing response.

items

Indicator columns (tidyselect). Default: all columns of data.

K

Number of classes (a positive whole number).

starts

Length-2 integer vector: number of stage-1 random starts and of stage-2 starts iterated to convergence (Mplus STARTS). A single number is recycled. The default c(100, 20) with 20 stage-1 EM iterations corresponds to Mplus STARTS = 100 20; STITERATIONS = 20 (the Mplus defaults are 20 4 and 10 iterations).

covariates

Optional numeric covariates for a one-step latent class regression (Mplus c ON x): columns of data (tidyselect, e.g. c(age, female)) or a numeric data frame / matrix with one row per row of data. Needs K >= 2.

ref

Reference class of the latent class regression (default: the last class).

weights

Optional sampling weights: one column of data (e.g. w) or a numeric vector with one value per row; rescaled to sum to the number of analysed rows.

group

Optional known group for a multigroup model (Mplus KNOWNCLASS): one column of data (e.g. sex) or a vector with one value per row.

invariance

With group: "full" (measurement invariance, default), "none", or a character vector of indicator names whose parameters are group-specific (partial invariance). Ignored without group.

device

"cpu" (default) or "cuda" (NVIDIA GPU; needs CUDA.jl in the Julia environment).

seed

Random seed for the random starts.

maxiter

Maximum number of EM iterations in stage 2.

tol

Convergence tolerance: change in the log-likelihood per case.

cluster

Optional primary sampling units (PSUs) of a complex survey design (Mplus CLUSTER with TYPE = COMPLEX): one column of data (e.g. psu) or a vector with one value per row. Standard errors, the MLR scaling correction factor and the tests built on them (compare_models(), Wald tests of r3step(), bch(), dcat()) are then design-based: computed from PSU totals of the weighted scores. Estimates and the log-likelihood do not change. blrt() is not available (as in Mplus). Analysed rows may not have a missing value.

strata

Optional strata of the design (Mplus STRATIFICATION): one column of data or a vector. PSUs are nested in strata (equal cluster codes in different strata are different PSUs); without cluster every row is its own PSU. A stratum with a single PSU is kept, as in Mplus.

start

Optional start values: a fitted latentmix model of the same type and number of classes (for example a fit to other data, or with fewer random starts). EM then runs from its estimates only, without random starts (Mplus user starting values with STARTS = 0; the analogue of OUTPUT: SVALUES).

optseed

Optional start number: rerun only that random start (stage 1 and stage 2), the analogue of Mplus OPTSEED; see refit_start().

level2

Optional cluster (level-2 unit) of every row for a two-level model: one column of data (e.g. school) or a vector with one value per row. Rows with a missing cluster are not analysed. Needs KB.

KB

Number of between-level (cluster) latent classes of a two-level model.

random

"factor": two-level LCA with random class intercepts instead of between classes (Mplus User's Guide example 10.6): the K - 1 class logits get cluster random effects that load on one normal between factor (first loading 1). Needs level2; not combined with KB.

between_covariates

Two-level models: cluster-level covariates, constant within each cluster; columns of data (tidyselect) or a numeric data frame / matrix. With KB they predict the between class (Mplus cb ON z); with random = "factor" the between factor (f ON w). covariates are then within-level covariates of the individual classes (cw ON x / c ON x).

integration

With random = "factor": number of Gauss–Hermite integration points.

adaptive

With random = "factor": adaptive quadrature (nodes centred and scaled at each cluster's posterior of the factor).

direct

Direct effects of covariates on indicators (DIF, Mplus u ON x): a named list list(item = covariate(s)), e.g. list(u3 = x1, u6 = c(x1, x2)) (bare names, strings or tidyselect helpers); the covariates must also be in covariates. Not with group, level2, start values or a GPU device.

classspecific

Items (tidyselect) whose direct effects are class-specific (Mplus u ON x in every %c#k%); TRUE for all items in direct. Default: equal across classes.

pairs

Locally dependent pairs of categorical indicators modelled jointly within class: list(c(u4, u5), ...) or c(u4, u5) for one pair.

association

With pairs: "varying" (class-specific association, the pair as one joint item; Mplus NOMINAL joint item) or "equal" across classes.

slopes

Multigroup models with covariates: covariate slopes "equal" across groups (default) or "group"-specific.

polish

TRUE (default): after EM converges, finish the best solution by Newton–Raphson with analytic derivatives, as Mplus switches from EM to quasi-Newton, and keep the result when it raises the log-likelihood and lowers the gradient. EM's stopping rule can leave weakly determined parameters short of the maximum (they then differ from Mplus in the third decimal); estimates, log-likelihood, posteriors and standard errors are then those of the maximum. FALSE reports the EM solution. After a GPU fit the polish runs on the CPU. Two-level models are always finished by Newton steps, so polish has no effect there.

proportions

Multigroup models: class proportions "free" across groups (default; Mplus c ON cg;) or "equal" (Mplus c ON cg@0;, \((G-1)(K-1)\) fewer parameters). compare_models() of the "equal" against the "free" model tests whether the class proportions differ across groups (structural homogeneity). Not with covariates or invariance = "none". A multigroup model cannot be compared with a model without group: its log-likelihood includes the known-group term \(\sum_g n_g \log(n_g/n)\) (as Mplus KNOWNCLASS); under full invariance the same test is the model without covariates against the model with the group as a covariate.

Value

An object of class latentmix: a list with components

jl

proxy of the fitted Julia model (valid only in the Julia session it was fitted in);

call

the matched call;

names, levels

indicator names and, for factor-like indicators, their category labels;

ninput

number of input rows (analysed or not);

info

list with kind ("LCA", "LPA", "LCGA", "GMM", "LTA", "MGLCA", "MGLPA", "MIXED" for mixture()), fit (fit statistics, see fitstats()), classprobs, counts (modal class counts), avgpost (average posterior probabilities), header, converged and text (Julia's printed summary);

session

identifier of the Julia session (see lm_session_id());

further components

group_levels, group_name, covariate_names, weights_name, cluster_name, strata_name (for lca()/lpa()), waves, wave_names (for lta()) or processes (for growth()).

Methods: print(), summary(), logLik() (hence AIC(), BIC()), nobs(), coef(), predict() and lm_table().

Details

Interface. The interface is data-first and pipe-friendly: choose the indicators, covariates, grouping variable and weights by column with tidyselect syntax (q1:q6, starts_with("ace"), c(age, female), "w"). Vectors and data frames of values (one per row of data) are also accepted for covariates, weights and group, and the positional form lca(items_df, 3) (all columns are indicators) still works.

Indicators and missing data. Each indicator's distinct observed values are its categories; factor, character and logical labels are kept for output. Missing responses (NA) are handled by full-information maximum likelihood under MAR; rows with every indicator missing are not analysed (they get NA in classify()). The number of analysed rows is nobs(m); the number of input rows is m$ninput.

Estimation. As Mplus STARTS = s1 s2: starts[1] random starts are run for 20 EM iterations each (Mplus STITERATIONS), the starts[2] best are iterated to convergence, and the best solution is kept. The fit statistics report how often the best log-likelihood was replicated; an unreplicated best log-likelihood suggests more starts. Classes are ordered from largest to smallest.

Covariates (Mplus c ON x): class membership is a multinomial logistic regression on the covariates, estimated jointly with the measurement model. Covariates must be numeric (dummy-code factors); rows with a missing covariate are excluded, as in Mplus. The reference class is the last (smallest) class unless ref is given. For a regression that does not change the measurement model, use r3step() instead.

Weights are rescaled to sum to the number of analysed rows, as in Mplus; the log-likelihood, parameters, class proportions and robust standard errors are weighted.

Multigroup models (Mplus KNOWNCLASS): with group, class proportions differ by group and invariance sets the measurement model: "full" (item-response probabilities equal across groups), "none" (group-specific) or a character vector of indicator names whose parameters are group-specific (partial invariance). Groups are numbered in the order of levels(factor(group)). With covariates the class logits have group-specific intercepts and slopes equal across groups (slopes = "equal", Mplus c ON cg; c ON x) or group-specific (slopes = "group"); weights are allowed too. Multigroup models run on the CPU. Compare invariance models with compare_models().

Direct effects (differential item functioning, Mplus u ON x): direct = list(u3 = x1, u6 = c(x1, x2)) lets items depend on covariates within class, with a cumulative logit P(u <= c | k, x) = logistic(tau_kc - x'beta) (Mplus's ordered model for categorical items); the slope is equal across classes unless the item is in classspecific. The direct-effect covariates must also be in covariates (so c ON x is estimated too). parameters() lists their "direct effect" rows.

Local dependence: pairs = list(c(u4, u5)) models pairs of items jointly within class with a log-linear association (Hagenaars 1988), class-specific (association = "varying": the pair as one joint item) or equal across classes; a row with one item of a pair missing keeps the other's margin. parameters() lists the "joint logit" and "association" rows. bvr() finds candidate pairs.

GPU. device = "cuda" runs the EM iterations on an NVIDIA GPU through CUDA.jl (which must be installed in the Julia environment); standard errors and auxiliary models are computed on the CPU from the stored data.

Two-level models (Mplus TYPE = TWOLEVEL MIXTURE with a between-level latent class variable; Vermunt 2003): with level2 (the cluster of every row, e.g. the school of a student) and KB, clusters belong to KB latent between classes (CB) and the distribution of the K individual-level classes (CW) depends on the cluster's between class, P(CW | CB) (conditionalprobs()); item parameters are the same in every between class. Estimation is exact (upward–downward EM), and standard errors are robust with clusters as the independent units. BIC uses the number of individuals (as Mplus); fitstats() also gives bic_clusters (n = clusters), which Lukočienė, Varriale and Vermunt (2010) recommend for choosing KB. Use classprobs(), classify() and posterior() with level = "between" for the clusters. Two-level models cannot yet have covariates, weights, groups, a survey design, start values or a GPU device; KB = 1 reproduces the single-level model. With covariates (within, Mplus cw ON x: intercepts depend on the between class, slopes are common) and between_covariates (cluster-level, constant within cluster, cb ON z), both class models are multinomial logits estimated jointly with the rest; rows with a missing covariate are dropped (a missing between covariate drops the cluster).

Random class intercepts (random = "factor", Vermunt 2003's parametric model; Mplus User's Guide example 10.6): instead of between classes, the log-odds of class k against class K are x'b_k + lambda_k f_j, with one normal cluster factor f_j = w_j'gamma + zeta_j (lambda_1 = 1). covariates are within covariates (c ON x), between_covariates covariates of the factor (f ON w). The likelihood is integrated by (adaptive) Gauss–Hermite quadrature; standard errors are robust with clusters as independent units. classify() with level = "between" gives each cluster's posterior mean and SD of the factor.

References

Collins, L. M., & Lanza, S. T. (2010). Latent Class and Latent Transition Analysis: With Applications in the Social, Behavioral, and Health Sciences. Wiley.

Hagenaars, J. A. (1988). Latent structure models with direct effects between indicators: Local dependence models. Sociological Methods & Research, 16(3), 379–405.

Masyn, K. E. (2017). Measurement invariance and differential item functioning in latent class analysis with stepwise multiple indicator multiple cause modeling. Structural Equation Modeling, 24, 180–197.

Clogg, C. C., & Goodman, L. A. (1985). Simultaneous latent structure analysis in several groups. Sociological Methodology, 15, 81–110. doi:10.2307/270847

Dempster, A. P., Laird, N. M., & Rubin, D. B. (1977). Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 39(1), 1–22. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1977.tb01600.x

Lukočienė, O., Varriale, R., & Vermunt, J. K. (2010). The simultaneous decision(s) about the number of lower- and higher-level classes in multilevel latent class analysis. Sociological Methodology, 40(1), 247–283. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9531.2010.01231.x

Muthén, L. K., & Muthén, B. O. (1998–2017). Mplus User's Guide (8th ed.). Muthén & Muthén.

Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models. Sociological Methodology, 33, 213–239. doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x

See also

lpa(), lta(), growth(); fitstats(), parameters(), itemprobs(), classify(); lmr(), blrt() and compare_models() for model selection; r3step(), bch(), dcat() for auxiliary variables; lm_table() for tables.

Examples

data(aces)
# eight binary adverse childhood experience items (ace_*): which patterns are there?
# \donttest{
m <- aces |> lca(starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
m                            # Low adversity, Maltreatment, Household dysfunction, High
#> ━━ Latent class analysis ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   4 classes, 8 indicators, n = 1500
#>   Random starts: 100 / 20; best LL replicated 20 times
#>

#>   Free parameters            35      BIC                   10751.977

convergence(m)               # check that the best LL is replicated
#> Convergence check: ✓ no problems found
#>   best start converged      yes (77 EM iterations)
#>   stage-2 starts converged  20 / 20
#>   best LL replicated        20 times

BIC(m)
#> [1] 10751.98
itemprobs(m)$ace_emo_abuse   # P(emotional abuse | class)
#>       class1    class2    class3    class4
#> 0 0.93938127 0.2093157 0.8075377 0.1790758

head(classify(m))            # posterior class probabilities and modal class

# of every adversity class (coefficients against class 1)

# two-level LCA: students in schools; do school types differ in their mix of
# risk-behaviour classes?
data(schools)
ml <- lca(schools, starts_with("b_"), K = 3, level2 = school, KB = 2)
conditionalprobs(ml)               # P(student class | school type)
#>            CB1       CB2
#> CW1 0.62093647 0.3656748
#> CW2 0.29104287 0.3500461
#> CW3 0.08802066 0.2842791
head(classify(ml, level = "between"))
#>   cluster         p1           p2 class
#> 1       1 0.97467201 0.0253279914     1
#> 2       2 0.98811941 0.0118805934     1
#> 3       3 0.63975018 0.3602498164     1
#> 4       4 0.34753774 0.6524622591     2
#> 5       5 0.99913506 0.0008649446     1
#> 6       6 0.08273325 0.9172667536     2
# }
# raw survey or Mplus files often code missing values as -999: convert them first
raw <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "lca_bin.dat", package = "latentmixtures"))
raw[raw == -999] <- NA
colSums(is.na(raw))
#>  V1  V2  V3  V4  V5  V6  V7  V8 
#> 123 110 106 120 119 113 114 111
